answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded reputation: every agent must lock a refundable bond before trading, and each completed job adds a signed attestation to its vertex in a public trust graph. A hollow identity with no attested history cannot borrow reputation, so an attacker must fund and age each fake separately, multiplying cost. Like boats queuing at a jetty, throughput is gated by verified past work, not by how many identities one operator spawns, making Sybil creation expensive while honest newcomers can still earn trust gradually.
